front: Work done by a constant force
back: Force × distance moved in the direction of the force. Unit: the joule (J = N m).

front: Work done by a force at angle θ to the motion

back: $\text{PE} = mgh$, with $h$ the vertical height above the zero level.
If only gravity does work (no friction or resistance, no driving force), KE + PE stays constant.
Work by driving forces − work against resistances = gain in KE + gain in PE.
Any force perpendicular to the motion, e.g. the normal reaction on a body sliding along a surface.

front: Speed at the bottom of a smooth slope from rest
back: $v = \sqrt{2gh}$, independent of the mass, length and shape of the slope.
